info.title: bmo-discord
info.description: The Discord chat provider's own API: the loopback seam between its two processes, grouped by the resource each route acts on. The provider routes another unit calls are bmo-chat's, stated in its `docs/protocol.md` and `docs/openapi/provider.json`; this document states only what this repository adds. Every body that is a chat piece is a reference to bmo-chat's OpenAPI documents rather than a copy, so bmo-chat's document is canonical where the two disagree. Bodies are JSON with camelCase keys, times are integers of epoch milliseconds, and every non-2xx answer is the error shape with `code` and `error`.

bearer.description: The bearer every route takes, read from BMO_DISCORD_ROUTE_TOKEN (docs/boundary-api.md, 「Configuration」).

Heard.description: Whether the bot account's socket hears one thing now, and where it does not, why.

Hearing.description: What the bot account's socket hears beside messages (docs/discord.md, 「Typing and presence」).

PersonInRooms.description: One person's presence beside the rooms they stand in.

allOf.description: One person's presence, by their number in the provider's `people` space.

lastSeenAt.description: Epoch milliseconds; null where the platform names no moment.

state.description: Whether a person is reachable now, as the provider maps its platform's own states.

oneOf.description: At the platform now, busy or not.
Signed in but idle, or stepped away.
Not at the platform, or hiding being there.

PresenceInRooms.description: Whether people are reachable now, each beside the rooms they stand in; the service tells the people who stand in a room the receiving side listens to.

whole.description: Whether the list is every person the provider tells presence of.

200.description: Whether the gateway is ready, why not where it is not, the bot token unset where it is ready without one (docs/discord.md, The bot token), and its version.

schema.description: Whether a provider is ready, where it is not, why, and the provider service's own version.

fold.description: Fold where the dialect can; whether to fold is the sender's decision.

silent.description: A notice that must not buzz a phone.

anyOf.description: A web address or a file path the provider can read.
A file as it crosses the wire with no identifier of its own, as a send carries it.

items.description: One picture of an album: an address the provider can read, or the file itself.

bytes.description: A file's bytes: inline as base64, or the part of a multipart body that carries them. An answer that names a file without its bytes leaves the field out.

part.description: The name of the part of this multipart body that carries the bytes.

item.description: One sticker item of the platform's own, which the provider maps onto its platform's wire.

id.description: The item's own key on the platform.

imageUrl.description: The address the item's picture stands at.

pack.description: The key of the pack, set or product the item belongs to.

thumbnailUrl.description: The address of the item's small picture.

title.description: The item's title, or the title of its pack.

fields.description: A sticker to send: an emoji the provider picks a sticker for, or one item of the platform's own.

oneOf.description: An empty emoji takes the account's own reaction off.

accountId.description: The account the send goes out in; unnamed, the provider's own.

anyOf.description: Whose account speaks on a provider. One axis of a read mode; `ChatReach` is the other.

oneOf.description: The platform's official bot interface.
A person's account, read only; a send in the owner's own words goes out in it.
A person's account, answered in behind a prefix the caller supplies.
An ordinary account of the provider's own, held by no person.
No platform: the owner typing into the machine.

mode.description: The voice to speak with; unnamed, the provider speaks with the voice it answers the room by.

prefix.description: The words the answers carry before them in the `human-avatar` voice; ignored in any other voice.

replyToMessageId.description:
The message the send answers. Ignored by a provider that does not declare `replyTo`, and by every kind
that answers no message.

speaker.description:
Who speaks, where it is not the one the room is answered by, as the caller's opaque string. Taken only
by a provider that declares `speakers`.

tag.description: Returned on the inbound message that is the platform's echo of this send.

schema.description: A send the provider performed: the answer of `POST /sends`.

messageId.description: Null where the platform hands none back.

missed.description: The pictures of an album that did not go; empty where everything went.

items.description: A picture a send did not carry, by the address it was given as, with why.

reason.description: Why one picture did not go.

message.description: The English sentence, as the sender rendered it from the code and the fields.
The English sentence, as the sender rendered it from the code and the fields.
The English sentence, as the sender rendered it from the code and the fields.
The English sentence, as the sender rendered it from the code and the fields.

oneOf.description: The provider's own English reason.

message.description: The English sentence, as the sender rendered it from the code and the fields.

default.description: A refusal or a failure, in the error shape.

get.summary: One room as the gateway knows it

schema.description: What a provider knows of one room.

identity.description: The sender number the account's own words carry in the room.

kind.description: `owner` when the room is the owner's private chat on this platform, else `group`.

oneOf.description: The owner's private chat on this platform.
Any other room.

modes.description:
The voices the room is read by and may be sent in, each one of the declaration's modes; null where the
provider does not say, which stands for every mode the declaration lists. `human-reader` alone makes the
room read-only.

owns.description: Whether the room is one of this provider's.

privateTo.description: The sender number of the one person in a one-to-one with the account.

title.description: What the platform calls the room, or null where it cannot or will not say.

404.description: The number is not one of this provider's rooms.

get.summary: A room's members as the gateway lists them

200.description: The room's members, whole: a DM's recipient and the bot account, or a guild channel's bot account and every person heard writing in it whom Discord confirms is still in the guild.

schema.description: The answer of `GET /rooms/{roomId}/members`: the room's members, whole.

name.description: What the room calls the person.

person.description:
The person, as a number of the provider's `people` space, the sender number the room's messages carry;
null where the provider has given the person none.

statusMessage.description: The person's status line, or null where the platform gave none.

404.description: The gateway holds no members of the room, with the reason.

get.summary: The room to reach the owner in

200.description: The room to speak into to reach the owner unprompted, or null.

roomId.description: The room to speak into to reach the owner unprompted, or null.

schema.description: The error shape: a code to match on and an English sentence saying what went wrong.

code.description:
Why a request was not answered with success: it could not be answered at all, or it was refused. Every
code of the common wire format is here, beside the protocol's own.

oneOf.description: The body or the query is not the shape the route takes.
The token is missing or wrong.
The token is right but the caller may not do this.
No route answers this method and path.
The route is right, but nothing stands at the key the path names.
The member's state does not allow the change, or the key is taken.

The member stood once and never will again, so the caller lets go of it. As a refusal: the message is
one the platform no longer has, or will never let change again.
The body or a file is over the route's ceiling.
The service failed while answering.
A service this one called failed.
The service is up but cannot answer yet.
The platform would not give the files asked for.
Refused: the provider does not declare the capability the call needs.
Refused: none of the pictures of the send went.
Refused: the provider speaks as the room's own account alone, so it takes no other speaker.
Refused: the provider has no number in the room for the speaker the send names.
Refused by the platform, for the provider's own English reason.

get.summary: Whether the gateway has confirmed the owner's account

200.description: Whether the owner's account is confirmed (`ready`), why not where it is not, and the gateway's version.

get.description: Answered from the gateway's last confirmation of the owner's account with Discord (docs/discord.md, 「The owner's account」); answering it makes no call on Discord.

get.summary: What the bot account's socket hears beside messages
get.description: Answered from what the gateway holds; answering it makes no call on Discord.

200.description: Whether typing and presence are heard, and where not, why.

put.summary: One message handed over to the receiving side

schema.description:
A message as a provider hands it over, under the room and the number the route's path names. Nothing
platform-shaped crosses, and no file path.

album.description: The number of the first message of the send of several this one came in.

context.description: What the platform said about a message beyond the message itself.

metadata.description: The platform's own payload, opaque; nothing outside the provider reads into it.

spokenText.description: The words the person actually typed, where `text` carries a placeholder.

tag.description: The opaque tag of the send this message is the platform's echo of.

files.description: The files the message carries, where they are already gathered.

items.description: A file a message carried, as a provider hands it over or fetches it again.

bytes.description: Left out, and read as withheld, where an answer names the file without its bytes.

part.description: The name of the part of this multipart body that carries the bytes.

id.description:
The provider's identifier of the file among its message's files: the same each time the same file
crosses, and never shared by two files of one message.

anyOf.description: What a file a message carried is, as the platform showed it.

oneOf.description: A short video the platform shows in a circle.
A short looping video without sound, or an animated image.
A sound file.
A recording made in the room to be heard as speech.
Any other file.

kind.description: What the file is, as far as the platform tells; left out where the provider cannot tell.

gatherFailure.description: Why the files gathering promised could not be kept.

gathering.description: The provider is still gathering the message's files and sends them later in a `GatheredPatch`.

anyOf.description:
What a message is where it is no one's words but a line the platform said of the room: a kebab-case code
and the fields it carries, which a reader renders in its own words.

line.description: The line the platform said, where the message is one rather than anyone's words.

oneOf.description: The platform's official bot interface.
A person's account, read only; a send in the owner's own words goes out in it.
A person's account, answered in behind a prefix the caller supplies.
An ordinary account of the provider's own, held by no person.
No platform: the owner typing into the machine.

origin.description: Where a handed-over message comes from.

oneOf.description: A message a room said.
A message already handed over, changed: its words, its sender, or both.
A past message read back from a room, kept where the receiving side lacks it and waking nobody.

room.description: What the provider already knows of the room a hand-over came from.

identity.description: The sender number the account's own words carry in the room.

anyOf.description: Which kind of room one chat is.

oneOf.description: The owner's private chat on this platform.
Any other room.

privateTo.description: The sender number of the one person in a one-to-one with the account.

senderName.description: The name the platform shows for who said it.

text.description:
Its words, or a placeholder the provider wrote for what was sent; on a line, the sentence that says it
to a reader that does not render the line.

via.description: The key of the provider that took it in.

200.description: The receiving side held the message before.

201.description: The receiving side did not hold the message before.

default.description: The receiving side's answer, passed on in the error shape.
